sentence: This project tries to add a spatial coordinate to existing single-cell RNA sequencing techniques, giving single-cell resolution and genome-wide coverage.
This project studies how bacterial pathogens that cause catheter-associated urinary tract infections settle and persist in the catheterized bladder, and how therapeutics affect them.
This project tests whether an inhibitor of a metalloproteinase can make glioblastoma tumors more sensitive to chemoradiation.
This project studies how metal-containing cofactors like heme or iron-sulfur clusters let proteins and enzymes carry out different kinds of chemistry.
This project builds a computerized tool that finds adverse safety events in emergency medical services charts of children with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
This project tries to find out how macrophages in the placenta respond to infection by Group B Streptococcus.
This project studies which nanomaterial properties activate inflammasomes and how they do it.
This project uses several imaging methods to study how brain changes appear before symptoms in a murine model of Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies the role of keratinocytes and an ion channel in pain caused by chemotherapy.
This project tests engineered T cells armored with a fusion protein as a therapy for Merkel cell carcinoma, a skin cancer.
This project studies how circuits in the human hippocampus and cortex let people learn through statistical learning.
This project builds computational methods that help scientists understand how gene editing changes proteins and health outcomes.
This project builds a data management platform and tools that help researchers reuse infectious disease data.
This project builds computational methods to assemble pangenomes across a population and to work with private or controlled-access data.
This project focuses on how medicines to treat substance use disorder are discovered and developed.
This project studies how an inflammatory pathway drives clonal expansion in people with a rare disorder that can progress to leukemia.
This project develops high-density, long-term neural recording tools to help understand neural circuitry in the spinal cord.
This project uses deep learning to build model observers that mimic expert feedback when judging medical image quality.
This project builds 3D-printed glass micro-optical systems for biomedical and clinical imaging.
